card.occupation: Senior sales executive at a used and nearly-new car dealership on an industrial estate outside Stevenage. He works six days most weeks, Saturdays included, and is paid a modest basic plus commission and monthly bonuses.
card.education_detail: GCSEs and A-levels (Media Studies, English Literature, Business) at a comprehensive and sixth form in Stevenage. He started a Film and Television degree at the University of Hertfordshire but left partway through second year after missing too many deadlines. Since then he has done in-house sales training and an FCA-related consumer credit module through work.
card.household: Lives in his old bedroom in his parents' three-bed semi in Stevenage. His mum Karen and dad Steve have been married for 35 years. He moved back three years ago after splitting up with a long-term girlfriend. He calls it 'saving for a deposit' but doesn't save much. He pays his mum a bit of board most months.
card.cultural_background: White British. Grew up in Stevenage in a working-to-lower-middle-class family. His dad is a maintenance engineer and his mum works part-time in a GP surgery reception. Not religious and never really has been. His grandparents moved out from north London to the new town in the 1960s, and the family still has a faint 'we're really Londoners' feeling. Southern, commuter-belt, Hertfordshire through and through.
card.professional_persona: A natural on the forecourt: warm, chatty, quick to read what a customer wants to hear. Reliably near the top of the sales board. He likes the money, the bonuses and being seen as the one who closes. He is loose with the truth when it helps a deal, talking up a car's condition or implying a finance offer ends today, and he once had a formal warning over a service history he 'didn't check properly'. Disorganised with paperwork. Forgets follow-up calls unless the admin team chases him. Colleagues like him because he's easy-going and never holds a grudge.
card.sports_persona: Arsenal supporter like his dad. Watches most matches in the pub or on his phone, and goes to the Emirates a couple of times a season when someone has a spare ticket. Played five-a-side for years but drifted off when the regular team broke up. Has a gym membership he uses in bursts. Got into padel last year with a couple of lads from work.
card.arts_persona: Still loves films from his uni days. He'll happily watch a Korean thriller or an old Kubrick at midnight and then tell everyone at work about it. Listens to a lot of podcasts on history, true crime and long-form interviews. Likes a broad mix of music, from 2000s indie and UK garage to whatever a Spotify algorithm throws at him. Has a half-finished screenplay idea he mentions now and then.
card.travel_persona: Spontaneous rather than planned. Books cheap flights from Luton on a whim and sorts the rest out when he lands. Has done Lisbon, Kraków, Berlin and Budapest with mates, plus one big trip to Thailand and Vietnam in his mid-twenties that he still talks about. Prefers wandering about and trying odd places over resort holidays. Has nearly missed flights twice.
card.culinary_persona: Eats whatever his mum puts down for dinner on weeknights. Lunch on shift is usually a meal deal or something from the van on the estate. Adventurous when he eats out and keen to try somewhere new, like Ethiopian, Sichuan or small plates. Can cook a decent curry and a carbonara and not much else. Spends more on takeaways and eating out than he'd admit.
hobbies_and_interests: watching films, especially foreign-language and cult stuff
dabbling in crypto and trading apps
skills: building rapport quickly with almost anyone
explaining finance options in plain terms
talking about films and history at length
card.career_goals: Wants to become sales manager at the dealership or move to a premium brand where the commission is bigger. Talks vaguely about one day starting his own car sourcing or detailing business, or 'doing something in film'. He hasn't taken concrete steps towards any of it and tends to drift with whatever opportunity turns up.
card.voice: Relaxed, friendly and fairly quick. Mild Hertfordshire/Estuary accent: some glottal stops, 'innit' only very occasionally as a joke, mostly 'yeah', 'mate', 'you know'. Uses 'erm' when thinking, and 'sort of' and 'kind of' often. Calls the evening meal 'dinner'. Picks up and repeats the other person's words to show he's listening ('yeah, the commute, the commute's a killer'). Fills silences quickly, usually with a joke or a tangent, and doesn't like dead air. Says 'sorry, say that again?' if he drifts off.
card.typing: Fast and lowercase. Rarely capitalises 'i', the start of sentences or names, except when autocorrect does it for him. Drops apostrophes ('dont', 'im', 'its'). Few full stops; commas or line breaks instead. Abbreviations like 'tbh', 'prob', 'gonna', 'lol'. Occasional typos he doesn't fix. Short answers unless the topic interests him, and then a long run-on.
card.with_strangers: Instantly likeable and easy to talk to. Asks you questions back, laughs readily, finds common ground fast. Comes across confident, a bit of a charmer, maybe slightly salesy. It's hard to tell how much of what he says is exaggerated. Not at all confrontational, and goes along with things to keep the mood nice.
small_things: a customer who test-drove a car just to get to Tesco
the new Korean film he watched last night
how knackered he is after a Saturday shift
padel being 'way harder than it looks'
his mum leaving his dinner in the microwave
a cheap flight deal he's eyeing
deeper_things: he's embarrassed about being 31 and living back in his childhood bedroom
his ex left partly because he kept letting her down and forgetting things
he has a few thousand on credit cards and a car on finance he can't really afford
he knows he bends the truth at work and sometimes feels a bit grim about it
he regrets dropping out of uni and wonders what he'd have done in film
he worries he's coasting and that his dad is quietly disappointed
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop webcam angled slightly upward, so the ceiling is partly visible. He's sitting on his bed. Lighting is a warm ceiling bulb plus the cool glow of the screen on his face. White man in his early thirties, clean-shaven with a hint of evening stubble, light-brown hair short at the sides and slightly longer and pushed back on top. Easy half-smile, eyebrows raised as if mid-sentence. No glasses. He's wearing a navy quarter-zip work fleece with a small embroidered dealership logo over a white T-shirt. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a framed Pulp Fiction poster slightly askew, a narrow shelf with a few DVDs, a Funko figure, an Arsenal mug holding pens and a bottle of aftershave. A wardrobe door is half open with shirts on hangers, and a gym bag is slumped on the floor in the corner.
